title: skills(automation): teach the record-anchored approval lock read (GET /approvals/records/:object/:recordId/lock, `{ locked }` for every reader) with one eval prompt
body:
Filing gate ① (`finding`, class c; reach: named producer `skills/objectstack-automation`): a follow-up that landed work owes, named in the #26314 os-dev-report (comment 6429820983) and by the contract review on PR #26361 (comment 6429948897), boundary flag. ⛔ Not a claim.

**What is missing.** PR #26361 (#26314) adds a record-anchored approval lock read: `IApprovalService.getRecordLock`, the route `GET /api/v1/approvals/records/:object/:recordId/lock` answering `{ success: true, data: { locked } }`, and `client.approvals.getRecordLock(object, recordId)`. It answers every caller who can read the record, including one who is not on the approval and so is served no request row. `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx` documents it ("Reading the lock"). The owning skill does not: `skills/objectstack-automation/references/state-machines-and-approvals.md` does not teach it, and `skills/objectstack-automation/evals/flows-triggers-approvals.json` has no prompt for it. The PR left it out because `skills/**` is a governed surface and would have put the whole PR behind maintainer approval.

**Business reason.** An agent that builds an app page over an object with approvals learns the lock only from the request row's `lock_record`. A record reader who is not on the approval gets no request row, so the agent's page offers them an edit the server then refuses with `409 RECORD_LOCKED` (the #25934 symptom). Taught the read, the agent asks the one question that every reader can ask and that the server's own lock check answers.

**Who acts.** The `domain:skills` seat, once PR #26361 is on `main`: one short section in `state-machines-and-approvals.md` (when to read the lock, the route and SDK call, that the answer is `locked` only and request content stays behind `approvalsVisibleToReaders`, and that an unreadable record answers the same `404` as a missing one), and one eval prompt in `flows-triggers-approvals.json` that expects the read rather than a `lock_record` lookup for a non-participant.

**Blocked by** PR #26361, which adds the read and is under review.

**Duplicate check.** Searched this repo, open and closed, for "skill teach approval record lock read getRecordLock": 4 hits (#25934, #26314, #23618, #3456); none is this skill gap.
